novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal omits the closer finite-interference-CI comparator TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012 §4.3 (and its exact-CI follow-up RigdonHudgens2015), despite presenting finite-sample confidence intervals under partial interference.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:weighted-erasure-spread
soundness_flags.one_line: “Prior-averaged coverage” and expected length are undefined because no prior/joint law for the tilted V signs and K is specified; H_WE names a route but not the probability measure the assertion quantifies over.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines a design-based minimax MSE criterion, takes the infimum jointly over all designs and estimators, and derives conflict-graph upper and lower rate bounds; it does not formulate honest confidence-interval expected length.

The paper studies nonasymptotic ATE intervals and matching estimation-risk lower bounds under ordinary randomized experiments with potential-outcome pairs Y(0),Y(1); its design-based lower bound is root-MSE rather than honest interval length under interference.

source_verification_receipts.version: PMC author manuscript corresponding to Statistical Methods in Medical Research 21(1), 2012
source_verification_receipts.locator: §4.3, “Finite sample inference for a binary outcome,” Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article explicitly develops Hoeffding-type finite-sample confidence intervals for causal effects under partial interference in randomized trials, for binary outcomes and its group-randomized setup.
The article shows that even structural assumptions permitting unbiased estimation under network interference need not guarantee decreasing large-sample variance.

The preprint develops fuzzy randomized confidence intervals, discusses expected length, and gives a Bernoulli-trial example attaining a minimum maximum expected-length benchmark; it is not a heterogeneous weighted-erasure result.
